## Hypothesis history

- after step 11: Microtubule stabilizers 0.94, Microtubule destabilizers 0.01, Protein degradation 0.01, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.01, Eg5 inhibitors 0.01

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.94); key evidence e2, e4, e5, e8, e9.

Why: Bright bundled tubulin, high atlas match to taxol/epothilone, monotonic dose response.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Washout + phospho-histone H3 / live imaging to confirm reversible mitotic arrest and tubulin polymerization assay in vitro to distinguish direct stabilizer from upstream mitotic kinase.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top call is strongly favoured: tubulin bundling/texture rises monotonically across three independently acquired doses (tub_glcm_contrast z 6.3 at 0.001 µM → 62.9 at 0.03 µM → 108.2 at 1 µM; tub_mean z 9.3 → 22.3 → 25.1), visual description confirms thick bright bundles/asters, and the atlas is dominated by stabilizers (6/10 neighbours, mean similarity 0.89). Destabilizers predict the opposite direction; Aurora/Eg5 and protein-degradation runner-ups do not explain the interphase tubulin polymerisation signal or the atlas profile. Each dose is a single replicate, but the effect is enormous and internally replicated across the dose series, so a further replicate would not plausibly overturn it. Stated probability 0.94 is calibrated.

## Unblinding

Compound: **docetaxel** (PubChem CID [148124](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/148124))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor; Tubulin stabiliser

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

## Reflection

The call was driven by an unusually large and specific tubulin signal: tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2 at 1 uM with tub_std z=+32.4 and tub_mean z=+25.1, persisting at 0.03 uM and 0.001 uM with monotonic dose response rho=+1.00 for both tub_mean and tub_glcm_contrast. Visual description of thick bright bundles and atlas match of 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers made destabilizers, Aurora and Eg5 inhibitors quantitatively implausible because they predict opposite tubulin direction.

What was weakest was replicate and cytotoxicity evidence. Each dose was a single independently acquired well, so the dose-response used only 3 wells, and cell_count rho=-0.50 p=0.67 did not confirm accompanying loss. I also under-explained the large nuclear shape change nuc_form_factor z=-26.2 at mid-dose and low-dose nuc_eccentricity z=+12.2, treating them as secondary to mitotic arrest.

The minor atlas neighbours Protein degradation 2/10 and Cholesterol-lowering 1/10 were correctly downweighted to 0.01-0.03, but they show how texture alone can bleed into other classes. Unblinding to docetaxel with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser confirmed the direction of the inference was correct.

What was right:
- Prioritized high-dose well w_df2909f8b4 to reveal massive tubulin bundling texture tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2, tub_std z=+32.4, tub_mean z=+25.1
- Used mid-dose w_13ba1079c0 and low-dose w_e78232492c to show persistence and monotonic increase 6.3 to 62.9 to 108.2 for contrast and 9.3 to 22.3 to 25.1 for mean with rho=+1.00
- Sought visual describe_phenotype to separate stabilizer bundling vs destabilizer loss, which returned Microtubule stabilizers
- Used compare_to_reference_atlas 6/10 stabilizers to reject Microtubule destabilizers, Aurora/Eg5 which do not explain interphase polymerization signal

What was wrong or missed:
- Cell_count dose response over only 3 wells was non-significant rho=-0.50 p=0.67, so cytotoxicity/mitotic-arrest inference was weak and vulnerable to density variation
- Kept Protein degradation and Aurora/Eg5 at low probability longer than warranted by e2/e5; 2/10 protein-degradation neighbours and lower density could have misled without dose monotonicity
- Did not mechanistically integrate strong nuclear dysmorphia nuc_form_factor z=-26.2 and nuc_eccentricity z=+12.2, and relied on single replicate per dose with no additional well to test reproducibility

Proposed next experiment: Cell-free tubulin polymerization assay with purified tubulin plus cellular washout with phospho-histone H3 and live imaging to test for direct, reversible microtubule stabilization and mitotic arrest.

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [36876916](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36876916/): Structural insight into the stabilization of microtubules by taxanes. *Elife* (2023) — Taxanes stabilize microtubules through direct binding, consistent with docetaxel as a tubulin stabiliser (PMID 36876916).
- PMID [18068131](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18068131/): Taxanes, microtubules and chemoresistant breast cancer. *Biochim Biophys Acta* (2008) — Taxanes act on microtubules, reviewed in the context of chemoresistant breast cancer (PMID 18068131).
- PMID [17656560](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17656560/): Mechanisms of multidrug resistance: the potential role of microtubule-stabilizing agents. *Ann Oncol* (2007) — Microtubule-stabilizing agents have a role in mechanisms of multidrug resistance (PMID 17656560).
